reason: Fast Landing contract reconciliation for the base-owned WP-B M2 Facebook static contracts exposed while validating Electron successor PR #640. At exact head dd686d61ac84e7b040bae957d00ade9a9baaca7e, WP-B M2 run 32567236342 passed delegated implementation-branch authorization, syntax, workflow authority and bounded diagnostics and executed all 116 contracts on both Windows and Ubuntu. Each OS produced 114 pass / 2 fail, with only M2-FB-002 and M2-FB-003 failing in backend/tests/architectureClosureV2/wpB/mandatoryOperationAdapters.test.js because those historical assertions still require persisted WP-B identity in a signed URL query via appendPersistedOperationIdentity / requirePersistedAttemptQuery. Trusted main 347097a6946a37e9f7b373ab5e9817c7cee97c82 already contains the ordinary-merged #639 authoritative Facebook transport, which intentionally forbids persisted WP-B identity in Worker URLs and instead binds complete x-yance-wpb-* headers to the Ed25519-signed request through a digest suffix on x-yance-request-id. Reintroducing query identity would regress the merged security/privacy authority. Closure Matrix is complete with unknownBlockers=0. This authorization permits only the single base-owned M2 test path to reconcile its static contract to the already-merged signed-header/request-id binding while preserving fail-closed persisted-attempt identity, physical-route guarding, authenticateDesktop, media persisted-attempt propagation and the no-local-retry authority. No Electron file, Facebook production file, workflow, routing policy, scanner, dependency, schema or release candidate change is authorized.
